digest.component_or_area: inbound reconciliation — parent-field differ and snapshot fetcher
propositions: A parent removed in Jira is never reflected locally because fetcher.py omits absent-parent fields from snapshots and inbound_differ.py refuses to emit parent_id=None, so the two systems diverge silently and permanently.

Clearing a parent requires positive peer evidence (recorded baseline per ADR-0026 binding) to distinguish 'Jira observed without parent' from 'parent-map read failed or truncated', preventing accidental data loss when REST fails or pages truncate.

The managed_refs gate alone cannot decide whether to clear because it answers 'was this set locally' not 'did the peer ever have it', which caused the 63-ticket incident where local parents were destroyed despite never being pushed.
A fail-open parent-map read must never overwrite a good observation with 'no parent' in the baseline, or the next pass treats it as a deletion and the incident recurs by a longer route.

The differ emits a parent clear only when peer evidence confirms the parent was observed, snapshot explicitly records absence (key present, value falsy), and the clear is managed—all three conditions required to prevent silent data destruction.

Rollout is safe by construction: on the first passes after the fix, no binding carries recorded peer observations, so nothing clears until evidence accumulates as passes run and the feature self-heals into correctness.
